relations.definition: Expressed approval or joy toward a positive event involving others.
relations.embedding_query_text: congratulated: Expressed approval or joy toward a positive event involving others.

chosen_property.label: hasCongratulatoryPost
chosen_property.definition: A relation between an organization and a social media post expressing congratulations.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property matches Organization → SocialMediaPost for expressing congratulations.

candidates.label: upvoteCount
candidates.comment: An upvote count relation between a comment and the number of upvotes it has received. Also called positive votes, likes count, approval count. Examples: "Comment upvoteCount '15'", "Answer upvoteCount '100'", "Question upvoteCount '5'".

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: positiveNotes
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute providing positive considerations, highlights, or pros for a product or an item being reviewed. Also called pros, advantages, benefits, highlights. Examples: A product has positive notes like 'Excellent battery life'. A review has positive notes like 'User-friendly interface'. The service has positive notes like 'Responsive customer support'. Distinct from negativeNotes, which provides negative considerations.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: endorsee
candidates.comment: An endorsee relation between an endorse action and the person or organization being supported. Also called "supported entity", "beneficiary", "recipient of endorsement". Examples: "Endorse action endorsee 'Candidate A'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Charity B'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Product C'". Distinct from endorsers, which are the people or organizations providing the endorsement.

chosen_property.label: knows
chosen_property.justification: The 'knows' property directly represents a social acquaintance between two people.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: isAccessoryOrSparePartFor
candidates.comment: A product compatibility relation between a product and the other products for which it serves as an accessory or spare part. Also called accessory for, spare part for, compatible with, used with. Examples: A phone case isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'iPhone 15'. A replacement battery isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'Laptop Model X'. A camera lens isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'DSLR Camera Y'. Distinct from isConsumableFor, which refers to items that are used up.

candidates.label: includesAttraction
candidates.comment: An attraction inclusion relation between a tourist destination and a tourist attraction located within it. Also called contains attraction, destination attraction, features attraction. Examples: "A tourist destination includes an attraction like a museum.", "The city includes an attraction for historical sites.", "This destination features a famous includes attraction."

candidates.label: distinguishingSign
candidates.comment: A distinguishing sign relation between a differential diagnosis element and a medical sign or symptom that helps differentiate it from other diagnoses. Also called "differential symptom", "diagnostic indicator", "key symptom". Examples: "DDx element 'Appendicitis' distinguishingSign 'Right lower quadrant pain'", "DDx element 'Flu' distinguishingSign 'Sudden onset'", "DDx element 'Migraine' distinguishingSign 'Aura'".

candidates.label: signDetected
candidates.comment: A medical sign or objective indicator identified through a medical test. Also called test finding, detected symptom, medical indicator. Examples: `Blood Test` signDetected `MedicalSign: Elevated White Blood Cell Count`, `X-Ray` signDetected `MedicalSign: Bone Fracture`, `Physical Exam` signDetected `MedicalSign: Swelling`. Distinct from `symptom`, which is a subjective experience.

candidates.label: suggestedGender
candidates.comment: An indication of the recommended gender for an intended person or audience. Also called "target gender", "audience gender", "gender recommendation". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedGender unisex", "The audience specification includes suggestedGender female", "This product is for suggestedGender male."

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: geoCoveredBy
candidates.comment: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

relations.definition: Participates in or is present at an event or activity.
relations.embedding_query_text: attends: Participates in or is present at an event or activity.

chosen_property.label: memberOfOrganization
chosen_property.definition: A participation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with.
chosen_property.justification: Existing schema.org properties like 'performerIn' or 'attendee' do not fit Person → Organization.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

relations.definition: Begins a new phase or activity.
relations.embedding_query_text: starts: Begins a new phase or activity.

instances: Justin Herbert -> Justin Herbert's Training Camp Start

chosen_property.label: startDate
chosen_property.justification: The 'startDate' property matches the Person → CreativeWork (CourseInstance) signature for marking the start of a training program.

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: startOffset
candidates.comment: A temporal offset indicating the start time of a clip or action, measured in seconds from the beginning of a larger work. Also called "clip start time", "beginning offset", "time offset start", "seek start". Examples: "The video clip has startOffset 30 seconds", "The action's startOffset is 120 seconds into the recording", "This segment begins at startOffset 0."

candidates.label: jobStartDate
candidates.comment: An employment start date relation between a job posting and the anticipated date for a successful applicant to begin work. Also called start date, commencement date, employment beginning. Examples: A job posting has a jobStartDate of '2024-09-01'. A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'Fall 2024'. A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'as soon as possible'. Distinct from jobImmediateStart, which is a boolean flag for immediate availability.

candidates.label: availabilityStarts
candidates.comment: A date or time marking the beginning of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability start date, offer start, access start time. Examples: "Offer 'New Product' availabilityStarts '2023-11-01'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Pre-sale' availabilityStarts '2023-10-20T09:00:00'". Distinct from availabilityEnds, which marks the end.

candidates.label: jobImmediateStart
candidates.comment: An employment timing relation indicating whether a job position is available for an immediate start. Also called immediate start, urgent hire, start now, ready to begin. Examples: A job posting has jobImmediateStart set to 'true'. A job posting has jobImmediateStart set to 'false'. This position has jobImmediateStart as 'true' for qualified candidates. Distinct from jobStartDate, which specifies a particular date.

candidates.label: applicationStartDate
candidates.comment: An application start date relation between an educational or occupational program and the date when it begins accepting applications for an enrollment cycle. Also called application opening date, submission start date. Examples: "A university program's application start date is '2022-09-01'.", "The scholarship program's application start date is 'January 1st'."

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: pageStart
candidates.comment: The page number or identifier where a work (article, chapter, etc.) begins. Also called starting page, first page, initial page number. Examples: "Article X pageStart 135", "Chapter Y pageStart 'xiii'", "Report Z pageStart 1". Distinct from pageEnd, which is the concluding page. pagination is a general range.

candidates.label: coverageStartTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage begins. Also called: coverage start, reporting start time, live blog commencement. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage start time "2024-11-05T18:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage start time "2023-07-15T14:00:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage start time "2023-10-27T09:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageEndTime, which indicates when coverage concludes.

relations.definition: Has a formal or informal connection to an organization.
relations.embedding_query_text: affiliated with: Has a formal or informal connection to an organization.

chosen_property.label: affiliation
chosen_property.justification: The 'affiliation' property directly represents a person's formal connection to an organization.

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: practicesAt
candidates.comment: A professional affiliation relation between an individual physician and the medical organization where they practice. Also called works at, affiliated with, employed by, is a doctor at. Examples: Dr. Smith practices at 'General Hospital'. Dr. Jones practices at 'City Clinic'. The physician practices at 'Family Health Center'.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: subOrganization
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a parent organization and a smaller organization that is a part of it, such as a subsidiary. Also called "subsidiary", "division", "affiliated organization", "part of organization". Examples: "Google has subOrganization YouTube", "The university's subOrganization is the Computer Science Department", "This company owns several subOrganization entities.". Distinct from department, which is a more specific type of sub-organization.

candidates.label: hospitalAffiliation
candidates.comment: A hospital affiliation relation between a physician and a hospital they are affiliated with. Also called affiliated hospital, associated hospital, hospital connection. Examples: "A physician has a hospital affiliation with 'General Hospital'.", "The doctor's hospital affiliation is a major medical center.", "This physician is affiliated with a specific hospital."

relations.definition: Failed to achieve a particular award or recognition.
relations.embedding_query_text: not won: Failed to achieve a particular award or recognition.

chosen_property.label: hasNotWon
chosen_property.definition: A relation indicating a person failed to achieve an award or recognition from an organization.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property captures the 'not won' relationship between a person and an organization.

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: educationalCredentialAwarded
candidates.comment: An educational credential awarded relation between a course or program and the credential received upon successful completion. Also called "award received", "qualification granted", "certificate earned". Examples: "Course 'Introduction to Python' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program 'MBA' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Master of Business Administration'", "Training 'First Aid' educationalCredentialAwarded 'First Aid Certification'".

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: ineligibleRegion
candidates.comment: A geographical exclusion relation between an action access specification, delivery charge specification, demand, media object, or offer, and the region where it is not valid or available. Also called restricted region, excluded region, unavailable in, not valid in. Examples: An offer has an ineligibleRegion of 'Alaska'. A delivery charge specification has an ineligibleRegion of 'Hawaii'. A media object has an ineligibleRegion of 'EU'. Distinct from eligibleRegion, which specifies where something *is* valid or available.

candidates.label: nonEqual
candidates.comment: A qualitative value that is not equal to another qualitative value. Also called not equivalent to, different from, unequal to. Examples: "Value A nonEqual 'Value B'", "Color Red nonEqual 'Color Blue'", "Size Small nonEqual 'Size Large'". Distinct from equal, which indicates equivalence.

relations.definition: Was featured or participated in a media production or performance.
relations.embedding_query_text: appeared in: Was featured or participated in a media production or performance.

chosen_property.label: appearedInCreativeWork
chosen_property.definition: A participation relation between a person and a creative work they were featured in.
chosen_property.justification: Existing schema.org properties like 'performerIn' or 'byArtist' do not fit Person → CreativeWork for non-performance appearances.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: workPresented
candidates.comment: A presented work relation between a screening event and a movie, identifying the film shown during that event. Also called screened movie, film shown, featured film. Examples: ScreeningEvent workPresented "The Matrix", FilmFestivalEvent workPresented "Parasite", DriveInMovie workPresented "Jaws". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPerformed, which is for live enactments.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: byArtist
candidates.comment: A performance relation between a music album or recording and the music group or person who performed it. Also called "performed by", "artist of", "featuring artist". Examples: "Album 'Thriller' byArtist Michael Jackson", "Recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' byArtist Queen". Distinct from composer, which is the person who wrote the music, whereas byArtist is the performer.

candidates.label: workFeatured
candidates.comment: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. Distinct from workPerformed, which is a live rendition of a work, and workPresented, which is a specific presentation of a movie at a screening event.

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: actor
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.

candidates.label: partOfSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an episode, season, or clip and the creative work series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: An episode is part of a series. A season is part of a series. A clip from a show is part of a series. Distinct from partOfTVSeries, which is specifically for TV series.

relations.definition: Distributed or made available a piece of content or media.
relations.embedding_query_text: shared: Distributed or made available a piece of content or media.

chosen_property.label: sharedCreativeWork
chosen_property.definition: A relation between a person and a creative work they shared or distributed.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly captures Person → CreativeWork for sharing content.

candidates.label: sharedContent
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as an image, video, or audio clip, that is included or shared within a comment or social media posting. Also called embedded content, attached media, shared media. Examples: `Social Media Post` sharedContent `ImageObject: Photo of event`, `Blog Comment` sharedContent `VideoObject: YouTube link`, `Forum Post` sharedContent `AudioObject: Podcast snippet`. Distinct from `mentions`, which is a reference to another entity, not necessarily embedded content.

candidates.label: distribution
candidates.comment: A distribution relation between a dataset and a downloadable form of that dataset, available at a specific location and in a specific format. Also called "data download", "dataset version", "downloadable resource". Examples: "Dataset 'Census Data' distribution 'CSV file'", "Research data distribution 'Excel spreadsheet'", "Open data portal distribution 'API endpoint'".

candidates.label: contentUrl
candidates.comment: A location relation for a media object, providing the URL to its actual bytes or file. Also called "media URL", "file URL", "download link". Examples: "Image object contentUrl 'https://example.com/image.jpg'", "Video object contentUrl 'https://example.com/video.mp4'".

candidates.label: originalMediaLink
candidates.comment: A link to the original version of media content, such as a web page or a direct media object file, in a media review. Also called source media link, original content URL, primary media source. Examples: "Media Review A originalMediaLink 'https://originalsource.com/video123'", "Image Review B originalMediaLink 'https://archive.org/image456'", "Audio Review C originalMediaLink 'https://podcast.example.com/episode789'". Distinct from url, which is the URL of the review itself.

candidates.label: regionsAllowed
candidates.comment: A regions allowed relation between a media object and the geographical areas where its use is permitted. Also called allowed in, permitted regions, geographical availability. Examples: "A movie streaming service has regions allowed 'US, Canada'.", "A music video has regions allowed 'Europe'.", "A software download has regions allowed 'Worldwide'."

candidates.label: itemShipped
candidates.comment: A shipment content relation between a parcel delivery and the product(s) being transported. Also called shipped product, contents of shipment, parcel contents, delivered item. Examples: A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'a book'. A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'clothing items'. A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'electronic device'.

candidates.label: associatedMedia
candidates.comment: A media object that encodes a creative work. Also called: media encoding, embedded media, content media. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Song' associatedMedia 'AudioObject of Song'", "CreativeWork 'Movie' associatedMedia 'VideoObject of Movie'", "CreativeWork 'Book' associatedMedia 'eBook File'."

candidates.label: embedUrl
candidates.comment: An embed URL relation between a media object and the URL pointing to a player for that media. Also called "player URL", "embed link", "streaming URL". Examples: "Video mediaObject embedUrl 'youtube.com/embed/videoid'", "Audio mediaObject embedUrl 'soundcloud.com/player/trackid'", "Interactive content embedUrl 'example.com/interactive/player'". Distinct from contentUrl, which is the direct URL to the media file itself.

candidates.label: encodings
candidates.comment: An encodings relation between a creative work and the media objects that represent or contain it. Also called "represented by media objects", "has media representations", "media versions". Examples: "Movie 'The Matrix' encodings 'Matrix.mp4', 'Matrix.avi'", "Song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' encodings 'BohemianRhapsody.mp3', 'BohemianRhapsody.wav'", "Book '1984' encodings '1984.epub', '1984.pdf'". Distinct from encodesCreativeWork, which is the inverse relation (MediaObject -> CreativeWork).

candidates.label: encoding
candidates.comment: An encoding relation between a creative work and a media object that represents or contains it. Also called "represented by media", "media representation", "has media object". Examples: "Movie 'The Matrix' encoding 'Matrix.mp4'", "Song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' encoding 'BohemianRhapsody.mp3'", "Book '1984' encoding '1984.epub'". Distinct from encodesCreativeWork, which is the inverse relation (MediaObject -> CreativeWork).

chosen_property.label: releasedCreativeWork
chosen_property.definition: A relation between a person and a creative work they released.
chosen_property.justification: Existing schema.org properties like 'releaseOf' or 'releaseDate' do not fit Person → CreativeWork.

candidates.label: releaseOf
candidates.comment: A release of relation between a music release and the music album it originates from. Also called part of album, from album. Examples: "A music release 'Single A' is a release of 'Album X'.", "A digital track is a release of 'The Greatest Hits Album'.", "A vinyl edition is a release of 'Classic Rock Album'."

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: releaseNotes
candidates.comment: A release notes relation between a software application and a description of changes in its current version. Also called changelog, version updates, new features. Examples: "A software application has release notes detailing 'bug fixes and performance improvements'.", "A mobile app update includes release notes about 'new UI design'.", "A game patch has release notes describing 'balance changes and new content'."

candidates.label: recordLabel
candidates.comment: A record label relation between a music release and the organization that issued it. Also called issued by, released by, label. Examples: "An album release is on the record label 'Universal Music Group'.", "A single release is on the record label 'Atlantic Records'.", "A compilation album is on the record label 'Sony Music'."

candidates.label: albumRelease
candidates.comment: An album release relation between a music album and a specific release instance of that album. Also called album edition, release version, publication. Examples: "A music album's album release is its 'Deluxe Edition'.", "The album's album release is its 'Vinyl Remaster'."

candidates.label: albumReleaseType
candidates.comment: An album release type relation between a music album and its classification as a single, EP, or full album. Also called release format, publication type, record type. Examples: "A music album's release type is 'AlbumRelease'.", "The music album's release type is 'EPRelease'."

candidates.label: musicReleaseFormat
candidates.comment: The format of a music release, indicating the type of recording media. Also called release format, media type, recording format. Examples: "Album X musicReleaseFormat 'CDFormat'", "Single Y musicReleaseFormat 'DigitalAudioTapeFormat'", "LP Z musicReleaseFormat 'VinylFormat'".

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

candidates.label: catalogNumber
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a music release and its unique catalog number. Also called "release ID", "record label number", "product number". Examples: "Album release catalogNumber 'ABC-123'", "Single release catalogNumber 'XYZ-456'".

chosen_property.label: copyrightYear
chosen_property.justification: The 'copyrightYear' property (CreativeWork → Number) is reused in inverse as Date → CreativeWork to associate the year with the work.

candidates.label: yearBuilt
candidates.comment: A construction year relation between an accommodation and a number, indicating the year in which the accommodation was built. Also called construction year, built year, year of construction. Examples: Hotel yearBuilt 1985, ApartmentBuilding yearBuilt 2010, House yearBuilt 1950.

candidates.label: copyrightYear
candidates.comment: A temporal relation between a creative work and the year its copyright was first asserted. Also called: year of copyright, copyright date, first copyright year. Examples: "Classic Album" copyright year "1970", "Software Version 1.0" copyright year "2005", "Research Paper" copyright year "2022". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first publication or broadcast.

candidates.label: modelDate
candidates.comment: A model date relation between a vehicle and the release date of its model. Also called: model year, release date, version date. Examples: "Car modelDate 2023-09-01", "Motorcycle modelDate 2024-01-15", "Truck modelDate 2022-07-01".

candidates.label: byMonth
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the month(s) of the year on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "months of year", "monthly recurrence", "in month". Examples: "Annual conference schedule byMonth 10", "Quarterly report schedule byMonth 3,6,9,12".

candidates.label: vehicleModelDate
candidates.comment: A vehicle model date relation between a vehicle and the release date of its model. Also called model year, release date, version date. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleModelDate '2023-01-01'", "Car vehicleModelDate '2024'", "Vehicle vehicleModelDate '2022-09-15'".

candidates.label: yearlyRevenue
candidates.comment: A yearly revenue relation between a business audience and a quantitative value, representing the annual income generated by the business. Also called annual revenue, annual income, gross annual earnings. Examples: TargetAudience yearlyRevenue "$1M - $5M", BusinessAudience yearlyRevenue "over $10M", StartupAudience yearlyRevenue "under $500K".

candidates.label: termsPerYear
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating how many terms of study are offered per year within an educational or occupational program. Also called "terms offered annually", "semesters per year", "academic terms per year". Examples: "The program has termsPerYear 2", "The educational program's termsPerYear is 4 (quarters)", "This institution offers termsPerYear 3 (trimesters)."

candidates.label: yearsInOperation
candidates.comment: An operational age relation between a business audience and a quantitative value, indicating the number of years the business has been active. Also called business age, operational duration, years active. Examples: TargetAudience yearsInOperation "5-10 years", BusinessAudience yearsInOperation "over 20 years", StartupAudience yearsInOperation "under 2 years".

candidates.label: birthDate
candidates.comment: A date representing a person's birth. Also called: date of birth, birthday. Examples: "Person 'John Doe' birthDate '1980-05-15'", "Person 'Jane Smith' birthDate '1992-11-22'."

candidates.label: productionDate
candidates.comment: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."

relations.definition: A mutual agreement between two people to marry.
relations.embedding_query_text: engaged to: A mutual agreement between two people to marry.

chosen_property.label: engagedTo
chosen_property.definition: A mutual agreement to marry between two people.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property captures the engagement relationship between two people.

candidates.label: spouse
candidates.comment: A marital relation between two persons who are married to each other. Also called "husband", "wife", "married to", "partner". Examples: "John has spouse Jane", "Mary's spouse is David", "The couple includes a spouse relationship.". Distinct from colleague, which indicates a professional relationship, or parent, which indicates a familial relationship.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: sibling
candidates.comment: A familial relationship between two people who share at least one parent. Also called brother, sister, kin, family member. Examples: `John Doe` sibling `Jane Doe`, `Mary Smith` sibling `Tom Smith`, `Alice Brown` sibling `Bob Brown`. Distinct from `siblings`, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: children
candidates.comment: A familial relation between a person and their child. Also called "offspring", "son", "daughter". Examples: "John children Jane", "Mary children Peter". Distinct from parent, which indicates the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: broker
candidates.comment: An intermediary relation between an invoice, order, reservation, or service and the organization or person who arranges the exchange. Also called "arranged by", "intermediary", "agent". Examples: "Flight reservation broker Expedia", "Real estate service broker John Doe", "Stock order broker Fidelity". Distinct from seller or buyer, which indicate direct parties in an exchange, whereas broker facilitates it without taking ownership.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: acceptedOffer
candidates.comment: An accepted offer relation between an order and the specific offer(s) that were agreed upon and included in it. Also called purchased offer, confirmed offer, included offer. Examples: "A customer's order accepted an offer for a laptop.", "The order accepted an offer for two books."

candidates.label: colleagues
candidates.comment: A professional relation between a person and other persons who are their colleagues. Also called "co-workers", "associates", "professional peers". Examples: "John colleagues [Jane, Peter]", "Mary colleagues [Sarah, Tom]". Distinct from colleague, which is a singular form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: colleague
candidates.comment: A professional relation between a person and another person who is their colleague. Also called "co-worker", "associate", "professional peer". Examples: "John colleague Jane", "Professor Smith colleague 'https://example.com/prof-jones'". Distinct from colleagues, which is a plural form, though semantically similar.

chosen_property.label: subjectOf
chosen_property.justification: The 'subjectOf' property (Thing → CreativeWork) fits Person → CreativeWork for coverage in a creative work.

candidates.label: geoCoveredBy
candidates.comment: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: geoCovers
candidates.comment: A geo covers relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place completely covers another, meaning every point of the covered entity is within the covering entity. Also called: covers, encompasses, overlies. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo covers "City 'Paris'", "North America" geo covers "Lake 'Superior'", "City 'Springfield'" geo covers "House '123 Main St'". Distinct from geoCoveredBy, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: coverageStartTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage begins. Also called: coverage start, reporting start time, live blog commencement. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage start time "2024-11-05T18:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage start time "2023-07-15T14:00:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage start time "2023-10-27T09:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageEndTime, which indicates when coverage concludes.

candidates.label: variantCover
candidates.comment: A variant cover relation between a comic issue and a description of its variant printing cover. Also called alternative cover, special edition cover, variant description. Examples: "ComicIssue variantCover 'Bryan Hitch Variant Cover'", "ComicIssue variantCover '2nd Printing Variant'", "ComicIssue variantCover 'Sketch Cover Edition'".

candidates.label: includedInHealthInsurancePlan
candidates.comment: A health insurance plan inclusion relation between a drug and a health insurance plan that covers it. Also called covered by plan, plan coverage, drug coverage. Examples: "A drug is included in a health insurance plan.", "The medication is covered by an included in health insurance plan.", "This drug is part of a specific health insurance plan."

candidates.label: coverageEndTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage concludes. Also called: coverage end, reporting end time, live blog conclusion. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage end time "2024-11-06T04:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage end time "2023-07-15T19:30:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage end time "2023-10-27T17:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageStartTime, which indicates when coverage begins.

candidates.label: includesHealthPlanNetwork
candidates.comment: A health plan network inclusion relation between a health insurance plan and a network it covers. Also called plan network, covered network, network of plan. Examples: "A health insurance plan includes a health plan network.", "The plan covers an includes health plan network.", "This insurance plan features a specific network."

candidates.label: includesHealthPlanFormulary
candidates.comment: A health plan formulary inclusion relation between a health insurance plan and a formulary it covers. Also called plan formulary, covered formulary, formulary of plan. Examples: "A health insurance plan includes a health plan formulary.", "The plan covers an includes health plan formulary.", "This insurance plan features a specific formulary."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: partOfInvoice
candidates.comment: A financial relation between an order and the invoice that includes it for payment. Also called is included in, is billed on, is covered by. Examples: An online purchase order is part of an invoice. A service request order is part of an invoice. Multiple orders can be part of a single invoice.

chosen_property.label: resultComment
chosen_property.justification: The 'resultComment' property (CommentAction → Comment) fits Person → CreativeWork as a tweet (Comment) created by a person.

candidates.label: dateDeleted
candidates.comment: A temporal removal relation between a data feed item and the datetime it was removed from the feed. Also called: deletion date, removal date, date of removal. Examples: "Expired Job Posting" date deleted "2023-06-30", "Outdated Product Listing" date deleted "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z".

candidates.label: datePosted
candidates.comment: A temporal publication relation between a CDCPMD record, job posting, real estate listing, or special announcement and its online publication date. Also called: posting date, publication date, listing date. Examples: "Job Opening" date posted "2023-10-25", "Apartment for Rent" date posted "2023-10-20", "Public Health Alert" date posted "2023-03-01T09:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is a more general property for first publication.

candidates.label: geoCoveredBy
candidates.comment: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: replyToUrl
candidates.comment: A reply URL relation between user comments and the web address where a response can be submitted. Also called comment reply link, response URL. Examples: "A user comment has a reply to URL 'http://example.com/comment/123/reply'.", "A forum post has a reply to URL 'http://forum.com/thread/456#reply'.", "A blog comment has a reply to URL 'http://blog.com/post/789/comment'."

candidates.label: dateRead
candidates.comment: A temporal interaction relation between a message and the date/time it was read by the recipient. Also called: read date, message read time, recipient read time. Examples: "Email" date read "2023-10-26T10:30:00Z", "Chat Message" date read "2023-10-26T10:35:00Z". Distinct from dateReceived, which is when the message arrived.

candidates.label: commentTime
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for user comments, indicating the date or date and time when the comment was made. Also called "comment date", "posted time", "submission time". Examples: "User comment commentTime '2023-10-26T10:30:00'", "Review commentTime '2023-09-15'".

candidates.label: liveBlogUpdate
candidates.comment: An update relation between a live blog posting and a specific blog posting that serves as an update. Also called: blog update, live update, news update. Examples: "Election Live Blog liveBlogUpdate 'Candidate X wins state Y'", "Sports Match Live Blog liveBlogUpdate 'Goal scored by Team A'", "Breaking News Live Blog liveBlogUpdate 'Emergency services on scene'".

candidates.label: dateReceived
candidates.comment: A temporal arrival relation between a message and the date/time it was received by the recipient. Also called: reception date, message arrival time, delivery time. Examples: "Email" date received "2023-10-26T10:25:00Z", "Package Notification" date received "2023-10-26T11:00:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: comment
candidates.comment: A feedback relation between a creative work or RSVP action and a user-generated comment. Also called "user comment", "feedback", "review". Examples: "Article comment 'Great read!'", "Event RSVP comment 'Looking forward to it!'". Distinct from commentText, which is the text content of the comment itself.
